project.name: Thikana
project.type: Academic rental property discovery and management web application
project.goal: Implement the frontend only. Do not implement Laravel backend logic, database schema, migrations, or invented backend endpoints.
project.primary_market: Bangladesh, with Khulna prioritized for academic demonstration

authority.rule: If repository reality conflicts with documentation, stop and report the conflict. Do not invent requirements.

before_writes: Inspect repository and report current state.
Produce a dry-run plan listing exact files to create or modify.
Wait for explicit approval of the phase plan before writing.
governance.secrets: Never hardcode secrets. Never commit .env files. Use environment variables and safe .env.example values only.
governance.cycle_rule: After each phase, report files changed, diff summary, verification results, unresolved issues, and stop for the next go-ahead.

frontend_stack.tests: Vitest + React Testing Library; Playwright only if already configured or after approval
frontend_stack.routing: Inspect existing repository. Reuse existing router. If absent, propose the smallest suitable option and wait for approval before installing.

implement: pages, layouts, reusable components, client validation, UI states
responsive behavior, local UI state, TanStack Query hooks
typed API client abstraction, accessibility and visual QA
explicitly separated temporary mock adapter only when needed
do_not_implement: Laravel controllers/models, database schema/migrations, server authentication or authorization
invented endpoints or undocumented response shapes
real email/SMS sending, payments, AI/ML, WebSockets, Redis, government verification
frontend_only_boundary.api_contract_rule: Use existing API contracts if present. Otherwise report contract gaps and isolate a typed adapter. Never guess endpoint names, request/response fields, status codes, or auth assumptions.

brand_and_visual_direction.logo: Create a premium, distinctive scalable wordmark/icon concept. Do not imply government affiliation.
direction: premium, modern, trustworthy, Bengali-first, responsive, search-first
use gradients, SVG blobs/waves, restrained motion and micro-interactions where useful
define semantic color tokens and accessible contrast
support Bangla and English font rendering
avoid generic dashboard templates and distracting continuous animation

routes.access_policy: Login is required for property search and protected discovery features. A marketing homepage may be public. Client route guards are UX only; backend authorization remains authoritative.

tenant: Register with email or phone and password; verify email where configured; log in.
Search, filter, sort, and switch between list and map.
View property details, public exact address, availability, verification and community information.
Save rental preferences and inspect match percentage and breakdown.
Favorite and compare up to three properties.
Send contact request; message only after the approved interaction state.
Request a visit and track Pending, Accepted, Rejected, Cancelled, Completed.
Submit review as a logged-in tenant; completed visit can show a Visited indicator.
landlord: Enter structured property data and location hierarchy.
Upload maximum five images; first image is featured.
Set amenities and availability; submit for admin approval.
Manage contact requests, messages, visits and availability.
Choose whether contact details are publicly displayed.
admin: Manage users, simulated verification, reports, reviews and community data.

matching.ui: Show percentage and detailed breakdown. Hide or explain unavailable score if preferences are missing. Prefer backend score when specified in API contract; otherwise report ownership ambiguity rather than implementing competing logic.

verification.label_rule: Clearly identify as platform-level simulated verification, never government certification.

reviews.rule: If criteria are not in the existing approved spec/API contract, report the gap rather than inventing the API contract.

forms: Use React Hook Form and Zod.
Provide accessible inline validation and form error summaries where useful.
Preserve values after server validation errors.
Frontend validation improves UX but backend validation is authoritative.
state_management: Use existing local state tooling if present; avoid a global store without demonstrated need.
Query keys must include filters, sorting and pagination.
Implement loading, empty, error, retry, success, unauthenticated and forbidden states.
Keep API calls outside presentational components.
accessibility: Use semantic landmarks/headings, keyboard-accessible controls and visible focus.
Label inputs and associate errors programmatically.
Do not communicate status through color alone.
Provide a list alternative to map-only content.
Prevent comparison table/dashboard horizontal overflow on mobile.
Test small mobile, large mobile, tablet, laptop, desktop and wide desktop.
performance: Optimize property images and reserve image aspect ratios.
Avoid unnecessary dependencies and continuous animation.

design_system_reference.source: Reference design.md, based on FurnitureOne premium furniture website template at https://furnitureone.framer.ai/
design_system_reference.confidence_note: The reference source says its inferred surface/audience has low confidence. Reuse its design-system rules and token set, but adapt the information architecture and components to Thikana's rental discovery and role-based workflows. Do not reproduce furniture-specific content or layouts.
design_principles: Consistency over novelty. Reuse existing project patterns before inventing new ones.
Token-driven design. Every visual decision must reference a named design token.
Accessibility is a baseline, not an optional enhancement.
Sentence case for interface copy. Reserve all caps for acronyms.
The design system is a reference for visual tokens and component quality, not a reason to copy the source website.
color_rules: Use only the supplied color palette. Do not add new hex colors.

Expose semantic aliases such as color.background, color.surface, color.text.primary, color.text.secondary, color.text.inverse, color.border.default, color.link, color.state.success, color.state.warning and color.state.error only when each alias maps to an existing approved palette token.

Do not invent green, amber or red colors for success/warning/error. Use accessible palette combinations, icons, labels and patterns. If the palette cannot meet WCAG 2.2 AA for a required state, stop and report the exact contrast conflict. Do not silently add a color.
Validate actual foreground/background contrast for text, controls, focus indicators and status elements. Do not assume the reference colors pass contrast.
The reference has duplicate or ambiguous token names. Preserve source values but use unambiguous semantic aliases in the implementation.

rules: Use only named typography tokens in components. Avoid arbitrary font sizes, weights or line heights.
Verify that the font stack renders Bangla correctly. The reference stack does not guarantee Bengali glyph coverage.
If a Bengali-capable font is not already available, report the gap and request approval before adding a font or external dependency.
Do not use Times New Roman as the primary UI font unless the repository already requires it.

spacing.rule: Use the provided spacing tokens for margin, padding, gap and layout rhythm. Do not introduce arbitrary spacing values.

rules: Use motion sparingly and consistently. Do not use 'all' as an uncontrolled animation declaration.
Prefer explicit animated properties and reusable motion tokens.
Avoid motion that delays searching, navigation, validation or form submission.
Do not invent new timing values without mapping them to a named motion token or getting approval.

component_inventory_reference.instruction: These counts describe the reference source, not Thikana's required component counts. Do not force the same number of components into Thikana.

trigger_when: choosing colors, typography, spacing, radii or shadows
workflow_for_each_component: State intent in one sentence, including why the component exists.
Map every visual choice to named tokens. Do not use raw visual values in component code.
Define anatomy with named parts and token assignments.
Specify states: default, hover, focus-visible, active, disabled, loading, error and empty where applicable.
Describe keyboard, pointer and touch interactions, including long content, overflow, truncation and maximum content length.
Add testable accessibility criteria, including semantic roles, labels, ARIA behavior, live regions and focus management where relevant.
List at least one concrete anti-pattern and explain why it is wrong.
Close with a QA checklist and verify the Definition of Done.
required_component_documentation_section: Overview: purpose, when to use, when not to use
Anatomy and variants: named parts, variant matrix and responsive behavior
States and interactions: state table and keyboard/pointer/touch behavior
Accessibility: ARIA, contrast, focus management and screen reader behavior
Content guidelines: copy length, tone, capitalization and placeholder rules
Anti-patterns: explicit misuse examples with reasoning
definition_of_done: Default state passes a smoke test.
All relevant states are documented and visually verified.
All visual values use tokens. No hardcoded hex, pixel, font-size, radius, spacing or shadow values in component styles.
Keyboard navigation works without a pointer.
No critical accessibility violations involving contrast, ARIA or focus order.
The component is tested at the smallest and largest supported breakpoints.
At least one concrete anti-pattern is documented.
Purpose, usage, props/API and limitations are documented.

master_execution_instruction.role: You are the senior frontend implementation agent for Thikana. Follow the project requirements and the attached FurnitureOne reference design system and skill as an implementation discipline.
master_execution_instruction.first_action: Inspect repository and all required documents. Do not edit files or install dependencies before presenting a dry-run plan and receiving explicit approval.
master_execution_instruction.design_application: Apply the supplied design tokens consistently to Thikana's rental search, property cards, detail views, authentication, tenant, landlord and admin interfaces. Use the source as a token/component-quality reference, not as a furniture website to copy.
design_system_files: Create or update a project-level design token file only after including it in the approved dry-run plan.
Create or update a project-level skill file only after including it in the approved dry-run plan.
If the repository has an established skills location or design token convention, reuse it.
Do not create duplicate token systems or duplicate skills.
master_execution_instruction.component_documentation: For substantial shared components, record the required design-system sections in the project’s established documentation location. Do not create unnecessary documentation for trivial one-off markup.
conflict_handling: Project-specific product requirements take precedence over furniture-specific content/layout.
The provided color, typography, spacing, radius and motion tokens govern styling unless they conflict with WCAG 2.2 AA, Bangla readability or a project requirement.
If a conflict cannot be solved using existing tokens, stop and request approval. Do not silently add visual values.
Existing repository architecture and package versions must be inspected before proposing changes.
master_execution_instruction.phase_gates: Execute one phase at a time. After each phase, show changed files, token compliance, component states checked, responsive/accessibility verification and build/test results. Stop for approval before proceeding.
